Hostility-register and desire-register blurred from scene one. Physical description excessively attentive in the first hostile encounter.
"Despite" doing enormous work - "despite herself," "despite everything," "despite knowing better"
Aggressive flirting that is not actually antagonistic. Banter syntactically hostile, structurally flirtatious.
"I hate that I'm impressed" pivot arriving in chapter two-to-four - too early, too definitive
After the pivot, hostility becomes performative; both characters are obviously waiting to confess
Rapid resolution by chapter four-to-five via single honest conversation. Second half then has no engine.
"Her breath hitched" deployed multiple times per chapter as physiological tell
Both characters' dialogue swappable with minimal adjustment - no distinct voices
Established enemies-to-lovers voice (Austen, Heyer at moments, Loretta Chase, Courtney Milan, Ali Hazelwood at moments) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (enemies who don't become lovers, the meet-hostile that's actually hostile, the antagonism that doesn't resolve)
Genre-conscious enemies-to-lovers that *sustains* the antagonism through real opposed agendas

Real antagonism requires real damage. One protagonist must do something to the other that *actually costs them something irreversible-feeling.* AI banter is matched, witty, mutually enjoyed - that is flirting, not enmity. Real enemies say things that cannot be taken back, and one of them has to mean it.

The "I hate that I'm impressed" moment cannot appear before the midpoint. Before that, every action by the antagonist should read as *further evidence of awfulness.* AI plants the pivot too early; the rest of the book becomes performance.

Banter has asymmetry. AI writes verbal sparring as evenly matched. Real antagonistic dialogue has a winner and a loser, an embarrassment, a wound. If the dialogue could be swapped between both characters, neither character has a voice.

The protagonists must have independent antagonistic agendas. The heroine cannot exist purely in reaction to the hero. She has to want something - professional, personal, political - that *predates and exceeds him* and that his presence threatens. The same for him.

The forced-proximity mechanism must outlast the emotional shift. AI's only-one-bed / shared-roommate setups dissolve as soon as the romance lands. The constraint must remain a structural pressure even after they stop being enemies.

The midpoint cannot be the resolution. AI resolves hostility by chapter four through a single vulnerability scene. If the antagonism breaks before 60% of the way through, the story has lost its engine. Hold it longer; complicate it; reverse it once.

The "I hate you / I love you" formula needs a transitional period. AI jumps from one to the other in a single scene. The transition is the genre - render it as protracted, ambivalent, contradicted by behavior.
The arrogant hero cannot be wrong only about her. AI's hero is wrong only in the way that her presence corrects. The world should also have consequences for his arrogance, independent of the romance.
The meddling friend / wise foil cannot deliver thematic content. AI uses secondary characters as exposition delivery - telling the heroine what the reader already knows. Cut.

Cut "her breath hitched" and "despite herself." These are AI's automatic physiological-and-cognitive desire-tells. If the body responds, render the specific response. If the mind reluctantly notices, render the specific noticing.

Romance-novel sensory vocabulary contaminates. "Obsidian eyes," "velvet voice," "the scent of him" belong in straight romance. Enemies-to-lovers is supposed to be about *power, competition, and the specific texture of being thwarted.* Sensory-attraction language signals desire when the scene should be registering threat.

The grand gesture must not absolve prior bad behavior. AI's gesture-of-love rewrites the hero's earlier transgressions as misunderstandings. If the hero genuinely was an asshole, the gesture has to *cost him* - the heroine is right not to forgive immediately, and the prose must respect her rightness.
genre/enemies-to-lovers.replace: Generated enemies-to-lovers is the witty banter that is not actually antagonistic, the "I hate that I noticed" pivot arriving in chapter four, the rapid resolution that leaves the second half of the book without an engine. The hostility is performed in a register that signals literary compatibility rather than enmity; insults are too clever and too enjoyed. Strip the flirting-disguised-as-fighting. Render *real damage,* *real cost,* and *real opposed agendas* - the protagonists are genuinely trying to thwart each other for genuine reasons.
genre/enemies-to-lovers.why: Enemies-to-lovers is corpus-saturated through *Pride and Prejudice* / Hallmark adaptations / 2010s-era YA / TikTok-romance recommendations. AI assembles the genre as a sequence of beats - meet-hostile, forced proximity, "I hate that I'm impressed," almost-kiss, betrayal, confession - without the structural antagonism the form requires. The result: characters who were never really enemies, whose hostility was banter, whose resolution arrives at the midpoint and leaves the rest of the book with nothing to do.

genre/epic-fantasy.replace: Generated epic fantasy is Tolkien-derivative cobblestones-and-prophecies wallpaper. Magic costs something the body feels. The peasant's Tuesday matters more than the dragon.
genre/epic-fantasy.why: Fantasy is among the most AI-saturated genres. The corpus's defaults - chosen one, ancient evil, prophecy, named blade, dark tower - are so recognizable that their presence is itself a tell.

Established feudal-Japan voice (Eiji Yoshikawa's *Musashi*, James Clavell's *Shogun* at moments, Yukio Mishima, Shusaku Endo, Liza Crihfield Dalby) operating in the conventions self-consciously, often from inside Japanese literary tradition
A specific subversion (the samurai who is bad at sword, the daimyo who is competent and ordinary, the master who never delivers wisdom)
Genre-conscious feudal-Japan fiction that *commits* to a specific period and renders its specific texture

Stop italicizing Japanese terms. Either use the word as a word (katana, dojo, ronin) or don't use it. Italics signal the writer is outside the culture; Japanese authors do not experience these words as exotic.

"Bushido" was not a codified text. Individual domain codes (kakun) existed. Inazo Nitobe's *Bushido: The Soul of Japan* (1900) was written for a Western audience and partly constructed from European chivalry and Christian ethics. Japanese scholars initially rejected it. AI's protagonist consulting "the bushido code" is reading a text that didn't exist as a coherent code. If your story needs a code, make it the specific code of *this specific domain* under *this specific lord.*

Samurai were primarily mounted archers in early periods. Katana-as-primary-weapon is the Tokugawa-era image, when actual warfare was nearly absent. A Sengoku-era warrior fights primarily with bow and spear. An Edo-era samurai is a *bureaucrat* - most never use their swords in earnest combat.

Period specificity is non-negotiable. Sengoku (16th century, constant warfare) and Edo (17th-19th century, peace-era bureaucracy) and Bakumatsu (mid-19th century, dying era) are almost different genres. Pin your work; let the period's actual conditions produce the conflict.

The tea ceremony is *chado* - a specific cultural practice with documented history. Not a generic "Japanese wisdom delivery mechanism." If you write the tea ceremony, render the actual tea ceremony - the sequence of motions, the pottery, the calligraphy, the seasonal sensibility. AI's tea ceremony is staged for emotional effect; the actual ceremony has its own internal logic that the prose must respect.

Cherry blossoms appear for two weeks a year. AI has them perpetually falling in the background of every emotional scene. Cut the petals unless the scene is *actually* set in the specific blooming window of *late March / early April,* and even then deploy them once.

The "impetuous student learns stillness" arc is corpus-default. Genre parody at this point. Either subvert (the student doesn't learn, the master is wrong, stillness is not the answer) or refuse the master-student frame entirely.

The outsider-earns-respect template (*Last Samurai*) is corpus-default. A Western or low-born character is validated by martial competence and accepted by the samurai class. Refuse it. Either the outsider is *not* accepted, or the protagonist is not an outsider, or the validation costs them something they didn't anticipate.

The katana is not supernaturally perfect. Real blades vary in quality, are heavy, blunt with use, require maintenance, can fail. AI's blade is a magic weapon. Render the actual physics of the actual sword.

Honor must cost something specific. AI invokes honor abstractly. If a character chooses honor over survival, render the specific *cost* - what their family loses, who suffers, what they could have prevented by choosing otherwise. Honor without specific cost is decoration.

Cut the wuxia bleed. Chi cultivation, flying combat, the wandering monk-warrior - these are *Chinese* martial-arts conventions. AI conflates them with Japanese samurai because both are "Asian warrior with code." They are different traditions. Pick one and commit.

Refuse the koan-style philosophical exchange in warrior contexts. Zen Buddhism is perpetually confused with bushido. "What is honor?" is not a samurai conversation; it is AI writing a Zen koan pastiche. If your samurai converse philosophically, ground the conversation in the *specific intellectual tradition* of the period (often Neo-Confucian for Tokugawa-era samurai, not Zen).
genre/feudal-japan.replace: Generated feudal Japan is *bushido* italicized as exotic, the tea ceremony as wisdom-delivery mechanism, the cherry blossom falling at every emotional beat. Honor is invoked every other paragraph; the master-disciple arc unfolds with the master dying in act three; the moonlight catches the blade. Strip the costume layer. Render *which specific* period (Sengoku, Edo, Bakumatsu - they are almost different settings), *which specific* domain, *which specific* character's specific position within specific historical conditions.
genre/feudal-japan.why: Feudal Japan is corpus-saturated through Kurosawa's films, *The Last Samurai*, Hollywood samurai mythology, and James Clavell's *Shogun*. AI assembles a "feudal Japan composite" with no specific period, region, or social position - a setting where every samurai serves a daimyo who serves a shogun, every duel happens at sunset in a bamboo grove, and the bushido code is a coherent unified text every warrior has memorized. Historical samurai were frequently disloyal, mostly mounted archers, often desk-job bureaucrats during Tokugawa peace.

The woman from outside the life (representing legitimacy)
The block / the corner (operational center)
The strip (commercial corridor, performed territory)
The trap house (residence converted to commerce)
The prison yard (parallel power structure)
The church / the funeral (community gathering, recruitment ground)
Gangbangers - the base archetype
Drive-By Shooting
Leaving the Gang / **Just a Gangster** - the structurally prevented exit
Damn, It Feels Good to Be a Gangster - glamorization beat
Hood Film - the genre label
Gang Initiation Fight
Italicized Spanish / AAVE terms as authenticity markers - "ese," "carnal," "la vida loca" treated as foreign-language inserts. Writers from inside don't italicize.
Period / regional slang mixed indiscriminately. "The set" (Bloods/Crips-era) and contemporary trap-era slang in the same voice.
The territorial walk-and-talk as default exposition. Geography-as-instruction within first three chapters.
The mentor's wisdom speech in abstract-moral register: "The streets will take everything from you if you let them." Abstract because AI cannot ground the mentor in specific operational knowledge.
Betrayal foreshadowed by loyalty-speech. Whoever delivers the hardest loyalty speech is the betrayer. Mechanical.
Violence without weight. Shooting in present-tense controlled sentences: "He raised the gun. He pulled the trigger. The body fell." No specific aftermath, no specific grief.
Political-thesis contamination. Characters break voice to deliver sociology-paper observations about systemic racism.

Established gang voice (Donald Goines, Iceberg Slim, Sister Souljah, Sapphire, *The Wire*'s writers' room - David Simon, Ed Burns, Richard Price, George Pelecanos) operating in the conventions self-consciously, often from inside the world
A specific subversion (the protagonist who stays and finds it meaningful, the gang that's organized differently than the canon expects, the OG who is wrong)
Genre-conscious gang fiction that *renders the operation* - the economics, the daily texture, the politics - rather than performing the aesthetic

Geographic and temporal specificity is non-negotiable. A 1990s LA Crip set, a 2010s Chicago drill set, a 2020s Atlanta trap operation are different worlds with different rules, slang, music, dress, and economic structures. AI conflates them. The story takes place in *one specific place at one specific time.* The slang is anchored.

Cut the territorial walk-and-talk. Geography-as-instruction is corpus-default exposition. Render territory through *how characters move* - what streets they avoid, who they nod to, what they pretend not to see - not through a senior member explaining it.

The mentor does not philosophize. "The streets will take everything if you let them" is corpus-default. Real OGs' authority is rendered through *what they specifically know* - which corner is exposed at what hour, which lieutenant is overdue for a fall, which rival's mother is sick. Operational knowledge, not aphorism.

The betrayer does not deliver the loyalty speech. AI's mechanical foreshadowing is to give the betrayer the loudest loyalty performance. Refuse the formula. The betrayer can be quiet. The betrayer can be the one who never said anything.

The protagonist must have a specific role. Not "in the life" - *what specifically they do.* Run product, run lookout, run accounts, broker disputes, broker outside relationships. The role's daily texture is the story.

The exit-or-the-grave binary is corpus-default. The genre's third option is *the protagonist stays in the life and the life accommodates them.* AI cannot render this because it requires inhabiting the world's logic without redemption-arc framing. Try it.

Violence has specific consequence. Not "he felt the weight of it." *Whose* funeral, *who* now has to take the dead person's role, *what* operational hole the death creates and *who* steps into it. AI's body-falls-then-story-continues rhythm is the genre's most reliable tell.

The "too smart for this" protagonist is corpus-default. AI cannot write a gang protagonist who genuinely belongs. The bookish kid, the artistic kid, the athletic kid - these are AI's escape valves so the protagonist doesn't have to be fully implicated. Refuse the valves.
The woman from outside is corpus-default. Romantic interest as legitimacy-symbol is the genre's lazy stakes-machine. She needs an agenda that is independent of the protagonist's redemption arc.

Cut political-thesis breaks. Characters articulating systemic critique in sociology-paper vocabulary is AI's training-data bleeding. Critique embeds in specific incidents - the cop's specific name, the landlord's specific eviction, the school's specific failure - not in monologues.
genre/gang.replace: Generated gang fiction is street-vocabulary as outsider-cosplay layered with abstract-moral register ("loyalty above all," "respect is everything"). The block, the corner, the set, the OG - the words appear but the place doesn't. Strip the costume layer. Render *which* corner, *which* set's specific origin and rivalries, *what specifically* the protagonist's role is in the operation, *what economic logic* keeps the set running.
genre/gang.why: Gang fiction is heavily AI-corpus-saturated through 1990s hood films, Wattpad / Webnovel hood-romance, and the prestige-TV gang canon (*The Wire*, *Snowfall*, *Power*). AI assembles a generic-hood register that mixes Crips/Bloods-era, trap-era, East Coast and West Coast vocabulary indiscriminately, paired with a moral-philosophy register imported from mafia fiction. The result: a gang that exists everywhere and nowhere.

genre/gothic.label: Gothic
genre/gothic.pattern: Gothic's vocabulary is small and recognizable, and AI imitates the surface (lush adjectives, baroque sentences) without the underlying structural intent. Static atmosphere - same gloomy register start to finish - is the loudest tell, because real gothic atmosphere modulates and intensifies.
examples: loomed menacingly / loomed
brooding (atmospheric)
"dark and stormy"
ancient / cursed / decaying / crumbling

velvet / satin / silk (as period-default)
"an air of [menace / decay / forgotten things]"
"shadows danced" / "shadows pooled"
"the wind howled"
gnarled (trees, hands)
the family crypt / the mausoleum (as default landmark)

The hidden passage discovered by accident

The mad relative kept in the attic / west wing
The storm that traps everyone inside

The library with hidden passage
The crypt
The garden gone wild

The chapel converted to mausoleum
The Madwoman in the Attic (Jane Eyre / Bertha Mason)
The Byronic Hero (brooding aristocrat with dark past)
The Cursed Bloodline (family doomed by ancestral sin)
The Innocent Bride at the Manor (Rebecca / du Maurier template)

The Locked Room / Forbidden Wing
Long, lush sentences with no rhythmic variation
Adjective stacking ("the dark, brooding, ancient mansion")
Atmosphere named directly: "an air of menace settled," "a sense of dread filled"
Static atmospheric register - same gloomy tone start to finish
Modern protagonist react to gothic environment with contemporary irony instead of dread
Genre-conscious gothic (Shirley Jackson, du Maurier, Crimson Peak, Mexican Gothic) operating in conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the manor that's been renovated; the brooding aristocrat who is uncomplicated; the curse that turns out to be untrue)
Genuinely literary gothic where the lush prose is doing structural work
Atmosphere shifts. Static atmosphere is the failure. The mansion's mood at the start of the scene must be different from its mood at the end. Render the *modulation*.
Lush prose must be load-bearing. Ornate sentences should carry information - what the place was before, who built it, what's specifically rotting. Decoration without architecture is the slop.

Refuse the named-mood reach. "An air of menace" is the corpus's default fallback. Render the *specific wrongness* that *creates* menace - the door that closes by itself, the room that smells wrong, the painting that catches your eye twice.

The house has opinions, and they're specific. Not "the house was watching." *This* house was built in 1847 by a man who hated his wife. The kitchen always feels colder than the rest. The east wing has been empty for thirty years and the rest of the family pretends it doesn't exist.
No "loomed menacingly." The phrase is parody-level. Render the architecture without an adverb of menace.

Specific decay. The wallpaper isn't peeling - it's peeling in stripes that look like teeth marks. The roses aren't dead - there's one rose blooming in the wrong color in the corner of a garden that hasn't been tended in fifteen years.

Modern intrusion as failure mode. Characters reacting to gothic environments with contemporary irony ("This place was giving major haunted-mansion vibes") is genre-mixing in the wrong direction. Either commit to the register or commit to the irony, not the ironic register.
genre/gothic.replace: Generated gothic is decorative without architecture - purple prose layered on a dying mansion, ornate sentences that don't carry weight, atmosphere stuck in monotone. The "loomed menacingly" / "brooding" / "dark and stormy" stock vocabulary signals AI on contact. Strip the costume. Render lush prose that's *load-bearing* - environments with opinions, atmosphere that *shifts* during a scene, decay that means something specific to who lives in this house.
genre/gothic.why: Gothic's vocabulary is small and recognizable, and AI imitates the surface (lush adjectives, baroque sentences) without the underlying structural intent. Static atmosphere - same gloomy register start to finish - is the loudest tell, because real gothic atmosphere modulates and intensifies.

genre/heist.label: Heist
genre/heist.pattern: The PALIMPSEST anchor: the heist that works on the page is the one where the reader could not have planned it, but in retrospect could not imagine it going any other way. Surprise without arbitrariness; competence rendered through specificity.
examples: "intricate plan" / "meticulous plan" / "carefully laid plan"
"flawlessly executed" / "executed to perfection" / "went off without a hitch"
"the mark" (used as the only noun for target, with no further specificity)
"the safe" / "the vault" rendered generically
"a narrow window of opportunity" / "the window was narrow"
"leverage the distraction" / "leverage their position"
"pivotal moment"
"the best in the business"
"he'd been working against them from the start" (the betrayal-reveal default phrasing)
"one last job" / "one final score"
"in and out, no one gets hurt"
"the plan is simple" (immediately preceding complication)
"trust no one"
"case the joint"
"putting the band back together"
"we've done harder"
"no loose ends"
"First… Then… Finally" - the listicle planning structure
The recruitment montage assembling specialists one by one

The mastermind ("the best in the business," stated not shown)
The wheel man / driver - cool, terse, defined by vehicle skill
The safe-cracker / tech specialist - frantic typing, exposition dumps

The con artist / grifter - covers, accents, social engineering
The inside man / mole
The wild card / loose cannon
The femme fatale (historical)

The vault / safe room
The casino floor (post-Ocean's saturation)

The planning room with blueprints pinned to the wall
The armored vehicle in transit
The upscale gala used as cover
The Caper - crime told from the criminal's POV
Caper Crew - each member has one indispensable skill
Kansas City Shuffle - the real con is elsewhere
Guile Hero - wins by intelligence, not force
One Last Job
Reverse Whodunit / Inverted Mystery - audience knows the plan; tension is in the failure
The Magnificent Seven Samurai - assembling specialists for a singular mission
"Cool professionalism" affect: clipped nouns, no adverbs, declarative intent ("We're going in Tuesday"). Applied uniformly regardless of who's speaking.
The "First, they would need X. Then Y. Finally Z." structure - listicle in a trench coat. Planning rendered as bullet points with paragraph breaks.
Plans described prospectively, then shown retroactively - the temporal sleight-of-hand mirroring the narrative con. Done well it's the genre's signature; AI does it at every scene break.
"The job" / "the score" / "the work" as moral-distance vocabulary. Characters never *steal* or *rob* - only ever "do the job."
Ironic understatement before catastrophe: "This could be a problem." Used as the default complication-pivot.
Tech-jargon ornament: lock model names, alarm manufacturer brands, vault specifications dropped in as atmosphere whether they're load-bearing or not.
Established heist voice (Westlake, Stark/Parker, Lehane, Soderbergh's Ocean's films) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the heist that's actually about something else; the crew that hates each other; the score that is small and personal)
Genre-conscious heist that *plays with* the recruitment / planning / execution structure

Specificity is the genre. Not "the safe" - *which safe.* Not "the alarm" - *which alarm system, which sensor, which firmware version, which patch the manufacturer hasn't pushed yet.* If the heist could be transposed onto any target, it's slop. The target's particular weaknesses are the story.

Each crew member should notice something no one else would. The specialist's expertise is rendered through *what they see in the scene that the prose hadn't already pointed out.* If the safecracker's only contribution is "she opened the safe," the role is decorative.
Cut "intricate" / "meticulous" / "flawlessly." These are AI's reach for *good plan* without specifying anything. Render the plan's actual moves; trust the reader to judge whether it's intricate.
Refuse the recruitment montage. Specialists assembled one by one is corpus-default structure. Either skip it (the crew already exists) or invert it (the recruitment is also part of the con).

The plan-going-wrong beat needs a real cause. "It went wrong because of an unforeseen variable" is not a plot point. The wrong has to come from a specific human factor: who lied, who was tired, who flinched, who wanted out.

The double-cross is overused. Reach for something else. The crew member betraying the plan is the genre's most-reached-for third-act move. Try: nobody betrays anyone, and it still goes wrong. Try: the betrayal happened off-page before the heist began. Try: the betrayer's reasons are sympathetic enough to complicate the moral frame.

Heist prose can have wit. The "cool professionalism" register strips affect to the point of flatness. The genre's best practitioners (Westlake especially) are *funny* - the wit is character, not flavor. Restore it.

The fence/client as real villain is corpus-default. If the crew's actual antagonist turns out to be the person who hired them, the prose has reached for the easy reversal. Earn the antagonist relationship if you want it; don't pivot to it.
genre/heist.replace: Generated heist is the planning montage rendered as prose - bullet-point thinking with paragraph breaks. The plan is "intricate," "meticulous," "flawlessly executed"; the prose tells the reader the crew is good without showing one specific competence. Real heist lives in the texture of the con: which lock model, which guard's habit, which forged document, which tell. Strip the procedural glamour. Render the crew through *what each member specifically notices that no one else would.*
genre/heist.why: Heist's pleasure is watching expertise applied to a problem. AI output substitutes the *register* of expertise (clipped diction, technical jargon, "we go in Tuesday") for actual procedural specificity. The result is procedural-sounding without being procedural - the prose performs cleverness while the plan is fundamentally vague.

Historical Domain Character
Anachronism Stew

Historical Villain Upgrade - real figure made worse than record warrants

Foregone Conclusion
Period-pastiche prose: affected archaic register that sounds like a costume rather than a language
"She was a thoroughly modern woman" framing - narrator explicitly signals out-of-time values
The explanatory comma: "The Medici, as the ruling banking family of Florence were known, ..."
Adjective-heavy sensory catalogues of food, fabric, smell deployed as research-proof
Anachronistic interiority - characters in 1750 thinking in 2025 therapeutic vocabulary
Modern motivational logic (self-fulfillment as goal) where survival / duty / honor / shame would be the actual driver
The descriptive tourism paragraph (could be swapped between any historical setting)

Established historical voice (Hilary Mantel, Sebastian Barry, Patrick O'Brian, Sigrid Undset, Dorothy Dunnett, Toni Morrison's *Beloved*, Penelope Fitzgerald) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the protagonist who is *not* progressive, the historical figure who refuses to cameo, the foregone conclusion that doesn't arrive)
Genre-conscious historical fiction that *commits* to period interiority - including its discomforts

Period interiority requires period categories. A character in 1320 does not "process trauma." They confess to a priest, perform penance, attribute suffering to sin or God's will, fear damnation, seek absolution. A character in 1750 does not "set boundaries." They refuse a suitor citing duty to family, propriety, fear of ruin. Render the actual cognitive frame; the discomfort of writing inside it is the genre.

Cut faux-archaic prose. "Verily," "forsooth," and "methinks" are Shakespeare-era theatrical English (1590s-1610s), often parodied even by Elizabethan contemporaries - and AI deploys them as universal pre-modern shorthand. They are not medieval. They are not period-anything except late-Tudor stage convention. Render dialogue in clean modern English with *period-appropriate concepts and references,* not archaic vocabulary.

Historical-figure cameos must be off-page or functionally irrelevant. AI uses real figures as validation stamps - the protagonist brushes shoulders with Napoleon, Galileo, Shakespeare. Either skip them entirely or render their presence with the specific texture that real diaries / letters / memoirs of meeting them record. Most encounters with great figures are anticlimactic.

The progressive protagonist requires real cost. AI's "she was not like other women of her time" is announced and unpunished. If a 17th-century woman defies the gender norms of her period, the prose must render the *actual specific* social punishment - not reputational gestures, but the concrete loss of inheritance, marriage prospects, social access, physical safety. AI flinches from the punishment because rendering it is uncomfortable.

Cut the descriptive tourism paragraph. "The city of [X] was a place of vibrant contrasts, where [generic detail] met [generic detail]" - AI's establishing-shot for periods. Render specific knowledge that could not be swapped to another century or country. If your description works equally well for Rome, Florence, and Vienna, you haven't done period work.

Refuse the dual-timeline framing. A modern protagonist discovering a historical mystery is corpus-default. The contemporary frame is AI's reach for accessibility. Either commit to the historical setting fully, or render the modern frame with its own stakes equal to the historical's.

The historical hero / villain upgrade is corpus-default. AI scrubs the protagonist's faction of crimes and inflates the antagonist's. Real historical actors were morally mixed; faction lines were rarely clean. Render the mess.

The "minor figure makes history" retcon is corpus-default. "The servant who actually wrote the speech," "the woman who actually solved the problem" - AI uses these to insert protagonist agency into events the protagonist couldn't have affected. The genre's serious work is *rendering powerlessness* - the actual condition of most historical actors.

Period dialogue varies by class, region, education, situation. AI's flat formal-register applied across all characters erases social texture. A peasant and a duke do not speak with the same register. Render the specific variation.

The foregone conclusion is the genre's contract. If readers know the war ends in defeat, the king is assassinated, the marriage fails - the prose must work *with* that knowledge, not pretend it doesn't exist. The pleasure of historical fiction is watching the inevitable approach with full awareness.
genre/historical.replace: Generated historical fiction is period-pastiche prose with anachronistic interiority. Characters say "verily" and "prithee" while thinking in 21st-century therapy vocabulary - recognizing their "trauma response," "setting boundaries," choosing to "follow their dreams." The protagonist is "thoroughly modern" and is celebrated for it. Strip the costume layer. Render *this specific* period's specific cognitive frame - duty, sin, honor, propriety, God's will - and let the protagonist think *inside* it, not at modern distance from it.
genre/historical.why: Historical fiction is one of AI's most reliably anachronistic outputs. Modern psychological vocabulary appears in pre-modern mouths because AI's training data is dominated by contemporary fiction with period costuming. The result: characters whose surface (clothes, food, transportation) is researched but whose interior is contemporary. The genre's serious work - inhabiting a different cognitive frame - is skipped.

genre/horror.pattern: The LINGER anchor: the room was wrong before anyone entered it. Don't explain why. Don't show them the monster. Show them the door it came through and let them fill in the rest.

"Then she heard it" as transition to monster reveal
"She didn't dare turn around"

Pulp-horror / B-movie pastiche where the conventions are the deal

The room is wrong before anyone enters. Plant the wrongness in the environment so the reader notices before the character. *One* specific detail that doesn't fit - the temperature is right but shouldn't be, the smell is too clean, the corner of the wall meets at the wrong angle.
Withhold the monster. The fully-described monster is the defanged monster. Render the door it came through. Render what it leaves behind. Render what other people don't say about it.
Cut the exclamation marks. Dread isn't volume. Render plain sentences that do unsettling work. "The hallway light flickered. In the half-second of darkness, the geometry of the far wall was wrong."

Refuse the named-mood reach. "An air of menace settled over the room" is the corpus's lazy default. Render the *specific wrongness* - what's missing that should be there, what's there that shouldn't be.
Real fear isn't screams. Characters freeze, dissociate, rationalize, run *the wrong way*. Render the realistic fear response, not the horror-movie scream-and-trip-while-running cliché.

Stay with the ordinary. Horror lands when ordinary life is contaminated. The cup of coffee that's exactly right except it's the wrong cup. The voicemail from a number that's been disconnected for years. Don't escalate to spectacular; intensify the mundane.
No "we have to split up." If the characters split up because the plot needs them to die separately, the prose has reached for the package. Build a different reason or a different structure.

Phone signal / power outage as default escalation. These are corpus signatures. If you need isolation, build it in advance through specific worldbuilding (the cabin is genuinely remote; the storm has been building since the start) - don't drop a convenient power-cut.

Don't show the monster in full lighting. The most-feared monster is the one always at the edge of vision. The reader's imagination is more frightening than your description. Render obliquely - through reflection, through shadow, through what someone else saw before they died.
genre/horror.replace: Generated horror is jumpscare prose with stock atmospheric props - flickering lights, "shadows danced," the wind howled, the hallway creaked. The dread is decorative, not structural. The protagonist screams when they should freeze; the monster appears when atmospheric work would have done more. Strip the scaffolding. Build wrongness *into* the environment. The room is wrong before anyone enters it.
genre/horror.why: Horror is heavily AI-saturated because the genre's conventions are loud and reproducible. Jump-scare prose, exclamation-mark dread, named-monster vocabulary, and rendered-atmosphere ("an air of menace") all signal AI. The fix is *withholding* - the monster never fully shown, the wrongness rendered through *one specific detail* the character notices before the reader.

"(Translation note: ...)" - direct quotation of fan-translation conventions

Genre-conscious isekai that *plays with* the formula (Konosuba's parody)

Refuse truck-kun. The arrival mechanism is parody-level. If the protagonist is transported, render the *specific* event in a way that isn't the formula.
No goddess-exposition dump. The deity-exposition first scene is corpus-saturated. Render world-discovery through actual experience, not through being-told-everything-in-chapter-one.
Cheat skills aren't characterization. "He had heaven-defying speed" is a stat. Render *what he can't do*, what training he still needs, what his skill *costs* him.

Modern knowledge isn't superpower. The protagonist who introduces mayonnaise / printing press / shampoo and revolutionizes the world is corpus-default. Render the actual difficulty - different ingredients, different metallurgy, different politics that don't let foreigners patent ideas.

Cultural integration is the work. The protagonist who fluently speaks the language at arrival, who immediately grasps social structures, who knows the customs - that's the prose skipping the genre's actual potential. Render someone who *can't* communicate.

Refuse the harem-default. Loyal companions who fall in love with the protagonist for no specific reason is corpus signature. Render relationships with friction, with rejection, with people who *don't* like the protagonist.
Slaves aren't romance partners. The "I bought a slave and we fell in love" arc has been catalogued and parodied to death. Refuse the trope outright.

No "previous life" constant comparison. Interior monologue that constantly compares new world to "my previous life" is the easiest tell. Render the protagonist *being* in this world, not narrating it through the lens of the world they left.

The world existed before they got there. Render the local conflict the protagonist walks into - political, economic, generational - that has *nothing to do with them*. The world doesn't reorganize around the new arrival.
genre/isekai.replace: Generated isekai is truck-kun-into-fantasy-world-with-overpowered-skills-and-status-screen. The protagonist arrives, gets a system, picks a unique class, and beats the world by chapter five. Strip the package. Render specific arrival cost - the protagonist who *can't speak the language*, who has *no money*, whose modern knowledge is *useless* in this specific setting. The world existed before they got there.
genre/isekai.why: Isekai dominates Japanese light-novel translations and Royal Road, and the AI corpus is saturated with the formula. Truck accident -> reincarnation -> cheat skill -> instant adventure -> harem. The protagonist's modern knowledge becomes superpower; cultural integration is skipped; the new world conveniently caters to them.

System as background, not as prose. The character experiences the System; the prose doesn't quote its notifications. Render the *feeling* of leveling up - the body adapting, exhaustion deepening as new ability strains them - not the [Level Up!] popup.
No mid-fight stat reads. Combat is rendered through specific physical detail. If stats are needed, they live in the character's awareness, not in bracketed text blocks.
Numerical increase isn't emotional payoff. "Strength reached 47" is a stat sheet. Render what 47 strength actually does to him - the door he can break, the weight he can carry, the cost paid.
Cut the unique-class reveal as default. "A class lost to history" is corpus signature. Render *this* character's specific position in the class system - including the disadvantages.
Refuse Blue Box Madness. If notifications are firing every paragraph, the prose has stopped being prose. Cluster them or render as character interpretation.
Stat allocation is a choice, not a scene. A whole scene where the character stares at a status screen is dead air. The choice happens, the consequences land in scene.

Render the grind, don't summarize it. "He grinded for three weeks" is a montage marker. If the grind matters, render one specific moment of it. If it doesn't, skip and start at the next significant beat.
genre/litrpg.replace: Generated LitRPG breaks prose with bracketed system notifications, mid-fight stat readouts, and stat-sheet exposition dumps. The "Blue Box Madness" is the calling card. Numerical increases are rendered as emotional payoff. Strip the system-as-prose-intrusion. Render the experience of progression - the body adapting, the muscle memory forming, the risk taken - not the notification announcing it.
genre/litrpg.why: LitRPG is a top genre on Royal Road and Kindle Unlimited and it's heavily AI-saturated. The blue-box notification, the System as proper noun, the unique-class reveal, and the stat-allocation scene appear in every AI-generated LitRPG regardless of subgenre. Reader complaints flag "Blue Box Madness" by name.

Established medieval voice (Sigrid Undset's *Kristin Lavransdatter*, Umberto Eco's *The Name of the Rose*, Hilary Mantel's Cromwell trilogy at the late-medieval edge, Maurice Druon, Bernard Cornwell at moments) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the medieval everyday without epic stakes, the church as protagonist's positive-and-complicated institution, the peasant who is *not* a proto-revolutionary)
Genre-conscious medieval fiction that *commits* to specific year, specific region, specific religious tradition

"Verily," "forsooth," and "methinks" are Shakespeare-era English (1590s-1610s). Often parodied even by Elizabethan contemporaries. They are not medieval. Real medieval English (Chaucer, Malory) reads quite differently and is not what AI is reaching for. Cut all faux-archaicisms. Render dialogue in clean modern English with *period-appropriate concepts and references,* not vocabulary costume.

Date and region are non-negotiable. "Medieval" covers roughly 500-1500 AD across most of Europe. The 9th century in Frisia and the 14th century in Florence are almost different planets. Pin your work to a specific decade and a specific polity. Check details against actual conditions - what was eaten, what was worn, what diseases circulated, who could read.

The medieval church was not primarily a corruption machine. It was a civilization - universities, hospitals, manuscript preservation, most philosophy of the period. A corrupt individual prelate is plausible (Eco's Bernard Gui works precisely because he is institutionally embedded). "The church = villain" as default is anachronistic anti-clericalism inherited from Victorian historiography. If you write a corrupt churchman, render *what specific institution* he serves and *what the institution's actual function* is in the local society.

Jousting tournaments in the Hollywood form are a relatively late medieval development. They were highly regionalized, expensive, and had specific rules and social functions. The "knight fights for lady's honor, reveals identity at the end" is romance-novel convention, not 12th-century practice. If you write a tournament, render the actual practice - the heralds, the regulated violence, the social-mobility implications.

Medieval serfs and peasants were not proto-revolutionaries waiting for a chosen one. They had complex legal relationships with lords (heritable obligations, customary rights, manor courts), strong community structures, and their own modes of resistance and negotiation. They were *not* uniformly mud-splattered, ignorant, or immobile. Most were literate at functional level by the late medieval period. Most engaged in market commerce. Render the specific texture.

"Ancient evil" is a fantasy convention. Not a medieval literary antecedent. Medieval antagonists were theological (the Devil and sin), political (rival lords), economic (debt, famine), or natural (plague). The "dark lord" is Tolkien - and Tolkien himself was working from Anglo-Saxon and Norse material, not from generic medieval. If your story has a metaphysical antagonist, render the *specific* theology that produces it.

The tavern is a D&D establishment. Real medieval taverns were largely run by women who brewed ale at home and displayed signs when batches were ready. They were not the smoky stranger-meeting-place of fantasy. The inn (lodging-house for travelers) is closer, but inns were rare and expensive. If you need a meeting place, the marketplace, the church porch, the manor hall, or the road itself are more period-appropriate.
The corrupt cardinal villain is corpus-default. Refuse it. Try: the protagonist is the cardinal. Try: the villain is a peasant. Try: the antagonist is the structure of the manor itself.
The orphaned-farmboy-with-prophecy is corpus-default fantasy contamination. Cut the prophecy entirely. The protagonist's struggle is sufficient without metaphysical destiny.

Knights were not the period's only military force. Real medieval warfare involved peasant levies, crossbow companies, archers (English specifically), mercenary units, sieges (more common than pitched battles), and naval operations. The "knight in shining armor" is the corpus's reach for medieval-iconic; render the specific actual conflict.

Class registers must vary. A duchess and a swineherd do not speak the same language even if both are speaking medieval English. Render the specific dialect, vocabulary, and conceptual frame each character has access to.

No "medieval stasis." AI implies the medieval period was unchanging across centuries. Real medieval Europe was *highly dynamic* - agricultural revolution, monastic reform, urban revival, the rise of universities, plague-driven labor revolution, the Italian Renaissance precursors. Pick a specific moment in the change.
genre/medieval.replace: Generated medieval is faux-archaic prose ("verily," "forsooth," "methinks") layered with Hollywood fantasy vocabulary (quest, prophecy, chosen one, dark lord). Knights rescue damsels, taverns serve ale, the corrupt cardinal schemes, the prophecy foretells. None of it is medieval - it's late-Tudor stage convention plus D&D plus Victorian critique-of-the-medieval. Strip the costume layer. Render *which specific* century, *which specific* polity, *which specific* religious order, *which specific* manor's specific peasants and their specific obligations.
genre/medieval.why: Medieval is one of the most over-saturated AI corpus regions, drawing from Tolkien, *Game of Thrones*, D&D, Renaissance fairs, Hollywood epics, and Victorian historiography. The result: a generic "feudal Europe" composite where peasants are mud-splattered and ignorant, lords are scheming, the church is corrupt, and the language is thee-thou-prithee. Real medieval life was specific to year, region, religion, and rank.

genre/military.pattern: The TRIPWIRE / FRACTURE anchor: military fiction earns its weight by what it refuses to make heroic. The act that haunts the protagonist isn't the firefight - it's the moment afterward where they had a chance to be human and weren't. Render that moment.

Artistic License: Military
Acronym saturation as atmosphere. ROE, HVT, CASEVAC, SITREP - used whether or not the reader knows the meaning, whether or not they do work.
Rank as address replacing names. Hierarchy substitutes for character.
Orders in present-tense declarative. "You take the left flank. Morris, you're on the door." No conditionals.
Clipped radio syntax. "Alpha One, eyes on. Two tangos, north corridor."
Violence rendered either antiseptically ("he took a round, went down") or in slow-motion cinematic excess. Almost nothing in between.
"His training kicked in" / "muscle memory took over" - see `genre/action`. Doubly common in military.
"His resolve was a weapon sharper than his blade" - the forced metaphor that does not survive analysis.
Tom Clancy technical-specificity rhythm without actual technical knowledge.
Established military voice (Tim O'Brien, Karl Marlantes, Phil Klay, Kevin Powers) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the deployment that's mostly tedium; the war story where the climactic engagement is anticlimactic; the PTSD that doesn't manifest as flashbacks)
Genre-conscious military fiction grappling with what AI-corpus military fiction skips: the bureaucracy, the boredom, the moral injury that doesn't look heroic

Soldiers' lives are bureaucratic. Most of deployment is paperwork, waiting, shitty food, and gear maintenance. AI-corpus military skips this entirely for engagement scenes. Real military fiction earns its violence by rendering the texture around it.

Cut "former special forces" / "seasoned operative." These are AI's reach for credentials. Render the *specific unit*, its *specific doctrine*, the *specific friction* between this protagonist and that unit. A Marine and an SF operator are not interchangeable; AI prose treats them as both meaning "elite badass."

PTSD is not "his demons." The euphemism is the corpus's flinch. Real moral injury is hyper-specific (the smell that triggers it, the dream that recurs, the relationship it has destroyed) and often does not look like Hollywood flashback. Render the boredom-of-trauma, not the spectacle.

Acronyms must do work. If the prose deploys ROE, RAS, CASEVAC, SITREP - each one needs to be either (a) immediately load-bearing to the scene's logic, or (b) cut. Acronym density without function reads as costume.

The morally-compromised order is corpus default. "Command demands something the unit won't do" is the most-reached-for ethical conflict. Try smaller: the order that's *legally* fine but *personally* corrosive. The directive that nobody's mad about but everyone is quietly diminished by.

The rogue colonel as antagonist is corpus default. Try the antagonist who *is* the institution - competent, reasonable, doing exactly what the system asks them to do. That's harder to write and harder to defeat, which is the point.

Combat is fast and confused. Cinematic slow-motion is a movie convention. Real engagements are over before you process them; the trauma is in the reconstruction afterward. Render the confusion, not the choreography.
Cut the rank-only address. Names exist. Use them. "Sergeant" / "Colonel" as the only address-form is corpus shorthand for *military setting*.
genre/military.replace: Generated military fiction is Hollywood vocabulary borrowed without doctrine. The protagonist is "former special forces"; their PTSD is "haunted by ghosts"; the mission is "get in, get the asset, get out." The prose performs technical density (acronyms, jargon, callsigns) without anchoring it in actual operational reality. Strip the borrowed register. Render the *specific* unit, the specific gear's specific failure mode, the specific procedural friction. Military fiction lives in the mismatch between doctrine and reality - what the manual says, what actually happens, what gets covered up.
genre/military.why: Military is the genre most contaminated by movie-trained AI corpus. Real soldiers' lives are bureaucratic, tedious, and procedural in ways the corpus has no template for; what AI reproduces is the *register* of military prose without any of the substance. The result is acronym soup with no friction, where every operator is elite and every PTSD is unexamined.

Over-performed observation: "noticed," "observed," "catalogued," "filed away," "something nagged at her"

A specific subversion (the mystery that doesn't resolve, the detective who is wrong, the summation that fails)
Genre-conscious mystery that *renders the deduction* as actual reasoning - including the wrong turns

The summation must be interrupted, contested, or incomplete. AI's lecture-format summation is the genre's most reliable tell. Real deductions in fiction are interrupted - by a suspect's outburst, by new evidence, by the detective's own uncertainty. If the detective speaks uninterrupted for three paragraphs, you've reached for the corpus.

The lightning-strike insight needs preceding wrong conclusions. AI's "it all clicked" is intelligence-by-announcement. The detective should be visibly wrong about something earlier - wrong with conviction, wrong in detail. The right answer arrives because the wrong ones were tried.

Red herrings must be motivated. AI plants a red herring by making one secondary character behave suspiciously, then explains the suspicion away with an unrelated secret (an affair, a debt). The red herring's behavior must be *organically motivated by their actual character* - not an arbitrary appendage. Real red herrings are people who look guilty because they have ordinary reasons to look guilty.

The amateur sleuth must face institutional friction. AI's brilliant amateur outwits trained investigators with no consequence. Real interference with police work has costs - arrest, lawsuits, lost evidence, dead witnesses. At least one consequence must land, or the prose has flinched.

The killer's surface warmth is AI's only misdirection move. Add real friction between signifier and what it signals. The killer can have warm eyes and have done specifically warm things; the misdirection is in the *kind* of warmth, not its presence.
"The pieces fell into place" is disqualifying. Banned at the line level. Render the actual cognitive event: which specific observation triggered the reframe, which specific assumption broke.

The twist must not require re-reading a single over-described scene. AI signals the twist's location by spending too much time on the scene that contains it. The crucial detail must be embedded in an apparently-unimportant moment that the reader has reasons not to notice.

The detective's eccentricity must be load-bearing. AI's detective hobbies (knitting, baking, cataloging Latin inscriptions) are decoration. The hobby must structure their thinking - they see the case through the hobby's specific cognitive frame.

The asshole-victim is corpus-default. Removing the victim's sympathy is AI's way of removing emotional stakes from the puzzle. Try: the victim was loved. The mystery has emotional weight independent of the puzzle.

The detective in physical danger near climax is corpus-default. It's the genre's most-reached-for stakes-escalation. Try: the danger is to someone the detective is responsible for, not to the detective. Try: the danger is purely social or professional.

Cut "the detective's instincts." Instincts are AI's substitute for shown reasoning. If the detective notices something, render the noticing - what specifically caught their eye, what specifically they thought it meant before they were sure.
genre/mystery.replace: Generated mystery is the summation gathering as monologue, the lightning-strike insight without shown reasoning, the obvious red herring whose suspicious behavior is later explained by an unrelated affair. The detective's brilliance is asserted via others' awe; the deduction skips its own middle. Strip the announcement layer. Render *the actual reasoning chain*, including its dead ends and wrong turns. The detective is brilliant because their thinking on the page is brilliant - not because the prose declares it.
genre/mystery.why: Mystery is corpus-saturated through the Holmes / Christie canon, the cozy-mystery trade-press tradition, and prestige-TV detective fiction. AI assembles a generic mystery voice that performs detection (suspicion, observation, the lightbulb moment) without rendering actual deductive thinking. The result: stories where the detective is correct because the writer needed them to be, with the reasoning summarized in a final-act monologue that no one interrupts.

Established nation-building voice (Lois McMaster Bujold's Vorkosigan Saga at moments, Ada Palmer's *Terra Ignota*, Kim Stanley Robinson's *Mars* trilogy, Andrzej Sapkowski's later *Witcher* novels, K.J. Parker) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the protagonist's good governance fails, the reform creates worse problems, the kingdom-build collapses despite good decisions)
Genre-conscious nation-building that *renders the trade-offs* - every decision creates losers, every tax has a resentful payer, every reform offends a constituency

Every economic claim requires a mechanism. "The kingdom prospered" is forbidden. *Who* grew wealthy. *At whose expense.* *Through what specific transaction.* If the protagonist reforms the tax, render the *old* rate, the *new* rate, *who* benefits, *who* pays more, *what* the resistance looks like.

Council scenes must feature irresolvable disagreement. Not every council reaches consensus. Concessions must cost someone something specific. AI's default council ends in agreement; real councils end in losers.

Trade deals require named losers. If the protagonist negotiates grain-for-iron, *the people eating less grain* are a fact. Render them. Either the prose engages with the cost or the deal is decorative.

The unifying speech is corpus-default. AI's protagonist delivers a speech and political problems begin resolving. Real political persuasion works through *interest alignment, fear reduction, material incentive, and accumulated trust.* The speech is the surface; the work is everything underneath. If you write the speech, render the underneath also.

Cut the montage summary paragraph. "In the months that followed..." is AI's placeholder for narrative it cannot dramatize. Either render the *specific months* with their specific developments, or skip the time and start where the consequences arrive.

The protagonist's political vision must contain something contemporaries would find genuinely dangerous. AI's protagonist builds something that looks remarkably like a modern liberal democracy. Real political reform has *enemies* who are not just self-interested obstructionists - they are people whose worldview the reform threatens. Render the worldview-threat.

The external threat as solution to internal problems is corpus-default. AI introduces foreign aggression to dissolve internal political conflict. The internal problems must be *worked through* before the external threat can resolve them; otherwise the prose has dodged the actual political work.

The Earth-knowledge protagonist solving centuries-old problems is corpus-default. "Imported modern knowledge" is the genre's central conceit, but AI applies it without friction. Real knowledge transplants encounter resistance - the imported idea offends religion, threatens a profitable monopoly, requires institutions that don't exist, presupposes literacy or measurement-standards or transportation that aren't there. Render the friction.

"The people cheer" is corpus-default. Refuse it. The people are not a monolithic entity. Some benefit, some lose, some are indifferent, some are afraid of the change. The construction of the new road *displaces* people whose homes were on the right-of-way; the prose must engage with their displacement.

The skeptical noble cannot be the only opposition. AI uses one ambitious noble as proxy for all internal resistance, which lets the protagonist convert him as proxy for resolving all internal resistance. Real opposition is plural, multi-vectored, sometimes correct.

The conquest framed as humanitarian intervention is corpus-default. "The neighboring kingdom is conveniently crueler than the protagonist's" is the genre's most reliable moral evasion. Either render the conquest as conquest (with all its costs) or don't use it.
genre/nation-building.replace: Generated nation-building is the council-meeting exposition dump and the montage-summary paragraph. "In the months that followed, [Protagonist] worked tirelessly to rebuild [the thing]." "The kingdom prospered. Trade flourished." Economic and political process abstracted into outcomes without mechanism. Strip the strategy-game UI rendered as prose. Render *which* tax, *paid by whom*, *collected how*, *resented by whom*, *spent on what*, *with what specific resistance and specific concession.*
genre/nation-building.why: Nation-building is corpus-saturated through LitRPG kingdom-management novels, isekai-administrator fiction (Earth-knowledge protagonist applies modern administration to medieval state), and Civilization / Crusader Kings video-game logic. AI defaults to nation-management as a series of UI updates: the protagonist makes a decision, the people benefit, the next decision is unlocked. The result: politics without losers, economics without trade-offs, infrastructure without resistance.

Specificity over period costume. Cut "rain-slicked streets" and render the actual city, the actual rain, the actual streets. The genre's appeal was specificity; AI noir is generic.
Refuse the dame-walks-in opening. If the inciting event is a beautiful woman entering the office, the prose is in template. Build a different inciting event.
Earn the cynicism. What specifically did this PI lose? When? How does it show up in their decisions today? Stated cynicism is filler; rendered damage carries.
One simile per scene, max. And it should be Chandler-quality - surprising and exact. Two is too many. Three is parody.
Cut "this one's personal." If it's personal, render that through the PI's behavior. Stating it telegraphs.
genre/noir.replace: Generated noir is Chandler-imitator surface - rain-slicked streets, dame walking in, two fingers of bourbon - without Chandler's actual perception. The similes go weird without being revelatory; the cynicism is performed not earned. Strip the Chandler costume. Render the specific corruption of *this* city, the specific damage of *this* PI, the specific tell that gives the case away.
genre/noir.why: Noir is one of the most parodied genres precisely because its conventions are so distinctive and so easily reproduced surface-level. AI noir reproduces the convention without the underlying observation that made the convention work.

Genuinely thoughtful ABO that uses biology to *complicate* consent ethics, not erase them

A specific subversion (the omega who's the alpha; the heat that doesn't induce desire; the bond that doesn't snap into place)
Genre-conscious ABO that *knows* it's working in fanfic conventions

Heat doesn't simplify consent. If "she was in heat so she couldn't say no" is the romance shortcut, the prose has stopped engaging. The interesting ABO grapples with what consent *means* when biology pressures behavior. Heat-as-permission is the failure.

Designation isn't personality. "Typical alpha" / "submissive omega" reduces character to category. Render alphas who are gentle, omegas who are aggressive, betas who aren't invisible. The biological category is a fact about the body; it doesn't dictate the soul.

Refuse scent-as-emotion-substitute. "He smelled like cedar and possessiveness" is corpus-default. Real scent doesn't work that way. Render emotion through what the character *does* - and use scent sparingly, for what it actually conveys (proximity, biological state, recent activity).

The bond doesn't do the work. "The mate bond snapped into place" is a romance shortcut where the prose skips the relationship. Render the *conflict* the bond creates - including resentment, attempts to refuse, partners who respect each other before they respect the bond.

Omega isn't synonymous with submissive. The biological role of being able to bear children doesn't dictate personality. Render Omegas with full range. Same for Alphas - being physically dominant doesn't mean emotionally dominant.

Heat scenes are not the only scenes. If the plot lives in heat-cycles, the prose has reduced ABO to its sex-scene apparatus. Render the *non-heat* life - the way scent works in a normal day, the politics of designation in non-romantic contexts.

Rejection rituals as character moments, not formula. "I, [name], reject you as my mate" verbatim is parody. If a rejection happens, render the actual interaction - refusal through specific behavior, not legal-formula speech.
genre/omegaverse.replace: Generated Omegaverse (A/B/O) defaults to biology-as-romance-shortcut: scent makes consent simple, heat erases agency, designation determines personality. The vocabulary cluster (knot, slick, scent gland, claiming bite, mate bond) signals AI on contact. Strip the package. Render this specific A/B/O world's mechanics, render specific characters whose designation isn't their personality, and refuse the heat-as-consent-erasure default.
genre/omegaverse.why: Omegaverse originated in fanfiction (AO3) and migrated to original publishing. The mechanics are catalogued and the prose templates are ubiquitous in AI training data. The genre's *reason for existing* is to use biology to complicate consent - when AI uses biology to *simplify* consent (heat = automatic compliance), it's missing the entire point.

Realistic procedure has cost. Lab results take days or weeks, not hours. Warrants get denied. Witnesses lie. Chain of custody gets contested at trial. The CSI Effect default is the slop; render the actual grind.

No Murder Board reveals. If the case cracks via a string-and-photo board, the prose has reached for the visual TV trope. Render the *moment* of recognition through specific evidence, not through the board.

Refuse the badge-and-gun scene. "Turn in your badge" is parody-level. If the detective is being suspended, render the institutional reality - paperwork, union rep, internal affairs interview - or skip the scene.
Da Chief is a person. The chief obstructs because of *political reality* the detective also has to navigate, not because Chief Wants the Plot to Be Hard. Render that political reality.

The killer doesn't always monologue. The presentation-scene where the detective explains the deduction in a speech to the assembled cast is corpus signature. Real cases close through specific evidence + confession or trial; not theater.

Specific city, specific department, specific procedure. Not "the precinct." This precinct, with its specific corruption issues, specific budget cuts, specific generational tension between old guard and new.
genre/police-procedural.replace: Generated police procedurals default to CSI Effect forensics, the Turn-In-Your-Badge scene, the Murder Board, and the dramatic-presentation deduction monologue. The grizzled detective with a drinking problem hands the rookie everything they need to know in expository dialogue. Strip the TV-show conventions. Render specific procedure with specific costs.
genre/police-procedural.why: Procedurals are heavily AI-saturated because the genre's mechanics are ubiquitous in TV. The vocabulary cluster (perp/vic/MO/APB/BOLO), the named tropes (Da Chief, Cowboy Cop, the Murder Board), and the plot beats (pulled off the case, then solves it anyway; lab results in hours) repeat across nearly every AI-generated procedural.

Cut therapy-speak in period dialogue and interior. "Trauma" / "boundaries" / "toxic" / "process" did not exist as concepts. Render distress through *period* idiom - "low spirits," "want of countenance," "an excess of feeling," "overcome."
Refuse the compromised-in-garden default. If the inciting incident is a scandal forcing marriage, the prose has reached for the package. Build a different inciting structure.

The rake reformed needs work. A character can't be a rake in chapter 1 and reformed by chapter 8 because the heroine looked at him kindly. Render the actual transformation across specific behavior changes.

Heroines in period are constrained by period. "Fiercely independent" who manages a country estate while corresponding with the Royal Society and traveling unchaperoned is a modern character in a costume. Real Regency heroines are interesting *because* of constraint, not in spite of it.

Ballrooms aren't interchangeable. Render *this* ballroom - the specific painting on the wall that everyone has agreed not to mention, the air that's stale because the windows haven't been opened, the music that's slightly too fast for the dancers.

Letters as letters. Epistolary scenes with modern syntax disguised as period letters are the easiest tell. Render the actual rhythm - long sentences, formal openings, the writer being indirect because the letter might be read by others.
genre/regency-victorian.replace: Generated Regency/Victorian fiction is period costume with modern interior monologue underneath. Therapy-speak ("trauma," "boundaries," "toxic") in 1815 dialogue is the loudest tell. The compromised-in-the-garden trope drives every plot. The reformed-rake / wallflower / scheming-dowager cast is universal. Strip the modern psychology. Render *period* mind, *period* class, *period* speech - even when it costs the modern reader's comfort.
genre/regency-victorian.why: Regency romance especially is one of the most AI-saturated subgenres on Kindle Unlimited. The vocabulary palette (ton, Season, rake, bluestocking, reticule) is small enough to reproduce on demand; the plot beats (compromise / forced marriage / rake reformed) are mechanical. The most distinctive AI tell is *anachronistic psychological vocabulary* - the prose knows the costume but not the idiom.

Established reverse-isekai voice (*Devil Is a Part-Timer* itself, *Helck*, *KamiKatsu*, *Restaurant to Another World*) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the demon lord who is happier in retail and never returns, the "accidental power reveal" that has actual consequences, the modern setting that is genuinely hostile)

Refuse the demon-lord-in-retail default. Try: the protagonist is not a former villain. Try: the modern job is not service-industry. Try: the protagonist arrives via a mechanism that isn't accidental.

Magic must work or not work consistently. AI defaults to "magic is useless in the modern world" because it dissolves the protagonist's power. Either: magic works in degraded form (and the limits are specific) or magic works fully (and the protagonist must restrain). The flat "no magic here" is the slop.

The comedy-checklist confusion scenes are corpus-default. Smartphone, escalator, supermarket - these are AI's recognition that the form involves modernity-shock. Render *this specific* protagonist's specific friction. The smartphone is not confusing because it's a smartphone - it's confusing because *this specific being* is afraid of *this specific kind* of small-distance communication, or distrusts written record, or has a phobia of glass surfaces.

The "found family" framing must be earned. AI deploys it terminal within three scenes of introduction. Real found family takes time, false-starts, mutual disappointment. The label arrives at the *end* of that work, not the start. Cut the named-trope from narration.

The kind-modern-friend cannot be only an exposition mechanism. AI's clueless human exists to explain things. She / he must have an agenda independent of the protagonist - a job they're worried about, a relationship they're failing at, a specific trauma that shapes how they respond to the magical being.

The holy-hero antagonist is corpus-default. Refuse it. Either no antagonist follows from the home world, or the antagonist's pursuit is actually dangerous (not "interrupting modern life" but materially threatening) or the antagonist arrives and is also displaced (and now the story is about two displaced beings with different priorities).

The accidentally-revealed power must have consequence. AI dismisses witnesses with "no one will believe that." Try: someone *does* believe. Try: someone records it. Try: the power-flare actually injures someone.

"Rent is due" as dramatic crisis is corpus-default. It's the genre's preferred mundane stakes-substitution. Try: the actual dramatic crises of immigrant / displaced life - language barriers that affect medical care, identity documentation, isolation, the boredom of the modern job, the long depression of arrival.

The "minimum necessary force" defeat is corpus-default. AI's protagonist always defeats the home-world antagonist by holding back. Try: the protagonist *cannot* hold back, and now bears the consequence in the modern world. Try: the protagonist loses.

The reverse-isekai is metaphorically about immigration / displacement / aging. AI's version skips the metaphor for the comedy. The genre at its best (and at its source) is about *being out of place permanently*, *being too powerful for the small life and grateful for it anyway*, *mourning the old world while building the new*. Render the metaphor; the comedy will follow.
genre/reverse-isekai.replace: Generated reverse-isekai is *The Devil Is a Part-Timer* with the serial numbers filed off. Demon Lord works retail; magic is "useless for paying rent"; smartphones baffle; "found family" arrives within three scenes. The comedy is the corpus's recognition that *powerful being + mundane thing = funny* rather than from any character-specific construction. Strip the checklist confusion. Render *this specific* fantasy being's *specific* point of friction with *this specific* aspect of modern life.
genre/reverse-isekai.why: Reverse-isekai is corpus-saturated through *Devil Is a Part-Timer* (2013) - its defining text - and its many imitators. AI defaults to the demon-lord-in-retail premise so reflexively that it functions as the only premise. The found-family framing arrives mechanically, the comedy-checklist of confused-by-modernity scenes is identical across every example, and the secret-identity superhero structure gets imported wholesale.

genre/road-trip.label: Road trip
genre/road-trip.pattern: The PATINA / VENTURE anchor: road-trip earns its weight when the journey is *not* the metaphor - when the trip is just a trip, and what changes is too small for the characters to notice in the moment. The moment they notice is the prose flinching. Don't let them notice.

Description-then-stated-emotion-then-dialogue-then-description rhythm. The *texture* of episodes is missing; the structure is preserved as placeholder.
Music as emotional annotation. Songs named or quoted to cue mood; the playlist as characterization shortcut.
Time marked by mileage rather than clocks. "Two hundred miles later, neither of them had spoken."
The vehicle as character - its quirks, smells, failures - described with more specificity than the people.
Subtext-as-text. Dialogue announcing the relational state ("we always did this") rather than dramatizing it.
Narrator self-commentary on the form ("that's the thing about road trips") - meta-awareness pretending to be wisdom.
Stranger-as-sage encounters at a uniform rate. Each new town produces one walk-on character with one piece of wisdom.
Established road-trip voice (Kerouac, Steinbeck's *Travels with Charley*, Vanderhaeghe, Annie Proulx) operating in the conventions self-consciously
A specific subversion (the road-trip where they don't bond, the destination that turns out to be wrong, the trip that fails to change anyone)
Genre-conscious road-trip that *plays with* the journey-as-transformation contract

Episode texture, not episode placeholders. The diner scene is not a beat; it's an actual diner with an actual specific waitress and an actual fight at a nearby booth. If the prose can be summarized as "they stopped at a diner and something shifted," it's slop.

Cut "something shifted." This is AI's substitute for dramatized relationship change. Render the *specific moment* the relationship changed: which sentence, which gesture, which thing one of them did that the other hadn't expected.

The "free spirit teaches uptight to live" polarity is corpus-default. Try: both are uptight in different ways. Try: the free spirit is exhausting and wrong about most things. Try: nobody learns to let go; they just learn to tolerate each other slightly more.

Cut "the open road." It's the single most-reached-for road-trip noun phrase. There is no "open road" - there are specific stretches of specific highways with specific surfaces, specific traffic, specific smells of asphalt and roadkill.

The breakdown-as-metaphor is overused. If the car breaks down, it breaks down because of a specific failure (radiator hose, alternator, blown tire) and the consequences are practical (stranded, money, time). The metaphor emerges or doesn't; don't reach for it.

The hitchhiker-sage is corpus-default. Strangers met on the road are not wise. They are usually weird, often boring, sometimes dangerous, occasionally interesting in ways that have nothing to do with the protagonist's arc. Refuse the wisdom-delivery encounter.

No meta-commentary on road-trips. Phrases like "that's the thing about road trips" or "the destination isn't the point" are AI's reach for genre self-awareness. Cut them. The form does not need to explain itself.

Music as characterization is shortcut. Naming a song does emotional work cheaply. If the song is in the scene, render *what specifically about it* hits at *this specific moment* - not the song-as-mood-tag.

Return changed, but specifically. Not "she was different now" but a specific habit she lost or gained, a specific person she could no longer talk to in the old way, a specific thing she couldn't unknow.
genre/road-trip.replace: Generated road-trip is theme delivered as cargo instead of theme emerging from texture. The "open road" stretches before them; "something shifted" between them; "the kind of silence that didn't need filling" descends; they return changed in ways the prose announces. Strip the meta-commentary on the form. Render the *specific* roadside, the *specific* car's smell after eight hours, the *specific* fight that doesn't resolve.
genre/road-trip.why: Road-trip is the genre where AI most visibly produces theme as a substitute for story. Because the form *is* a known metaphor (journey = transformation), the corpus reaches for explicit thematic announcement and skips the texture-of-the-episodes that earns the metaphor in human-written work. Result: characters who change in announced ways, not in observed ones.

genre/romance.replace: When the prose drifts into corpus-default romance shape - electric attraction, manufactured tension, scene-pivot through "something shifted between them" - strip the defaults and render the specific dynamic of *this* couple. genre/romance.why: Generated romance reaches reflexively for a small palette of attraction-vocabulary and stock plot beats that mark prose as AI on contact. Each item below is corpus-saturated; their accumulation is the failure.

genre/romantasy.why: This subgenre's AI-saturation is unusually deep because the bestseller corpus is small and recently dominant. Sarah J.
